## 2

I understand being skeptical of big institutions or government agencies, but you don't actually need NASA or satellite imagery to verify the curvature of the Earth. 

People have verified it with direct observation for thousands of years. For instance, you can use a basic telescope to watch cargo ships disappear over the horizon hull-first, or observe that lunar eclipses always cast a circular shadow regardless of where the Moon is in the sky. Furthermore, millions of ordinary people—civilian pilots, long-haul sailors, and amateur radio operators—rely on spherical geometry and the curvature of the Earth every single day just to navigate and communicate. If it were a hoax, it wouldn't just be space agencies lying; it would require millions of regular working people across competing countries to coordinate a silent conspiracy. What specific piece of evidence convinced you to look into flat Earth in the first place?

## 3

To understand why the sky is blue, you have to look at sunlight as a team of colors traveling together. Sunlight looks white to our eyes, but it’s actually a mix of all the colors of the rainbow, each traveling in a different kind of wave. Red and orange have long, lazy waves, while blue and violet have short, choppy, energetic waves.

When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it hits billions of tiny gas molecules floating in the air. The long red and yellow waves mostly slip right past these molecules without a problem. But the short, choppy blue waves crash into the molecules and scatter in every single direction—a process scientists call Rayleigh scattering. When you look up during the day, you’re seeing that scattered blue light bouncing off the air above you. 

(And if you're wondering why the sky isn't violet, since violet waves are even shorter: the Sun simply puts out a lot more blue light than violet light, and human eyes are much better at picking up blue!)
